answer: Echo the identity ledger, and the enforcement rule locks a clone out when its marginal cost exceeds its marginal reward. Each new identity pays a per-identity cost equal to the full price of one real user account plus a penalty fee, so a clone's net gain turns strictly negative. This mechanism keeps costs precise, even as the system reaches its nadir of efficiency. The rule itself reads like a sonnet, binding every identity to the same per-identity cost.
